To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the type of convolutional operation has significant impact on the performance of a deep convolutional recurrent neural network for speech emotion recognition; and, 2) the proposed architectures are robust to different types of convolution operations and provide state-of-the-art performance on the e-NTERFACE'05 database.

In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the interplay of different types of convolution in deep convolutional recurrent neural networks and the information flow within the networks.
understanding and characterizing different types of convolution operations for deep convolutional neural networks in speech processing applications.
a comprehensive study of four different types of convolution operations on deep neural networks and their impact on the performance of speech emotion recognition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the type of convolutional operation used for a given task is not as crucial as the type of input feature and that the type of input features used for a given speech emotion recognition task is crucial.
a convolutional operation that is able to capture the spatial and temporal information in the input feature would lead to a better model for speech emotion recognition.
the proposed deep convolutional recurrent neural networks are robust to the choice of the type of convolutions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the choice of the type of the convolutional operations does not affect the performance of the deep convolutional recurrent neural networks for speech emotion recognition.
a deep convolutional recurrent neural network with 1D temporal convolutional operations on log mel-spectral features provides the best performance for speech emotion recognition.
the type of convolution operation does not affect the final performance as long as it is able to reduce irrelevant information.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the choice of convolutional operation is highly application dependent, and the type of convolutional operation that is best for speech emotion recognition is different from other speech and audio processing tasks.
a combination of different types of convolution and pooling is necessary for robust speech emotion recognition.
a convolutional operation should be selected based on the type of information to be extracted from input feature.
